title: EZH2 Mutation and Epigenetic Heterogeneity in B-Cell Lymphoma
content: In collaboration with the Shema Lab at the Weizmann Institute, we published new findings on how the EZH2-Y646N mutation reshapes chromatin states in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, using CyTOF-based histone profiling.

title: PyPAS: New Open-Source Tool for Positron Annihilation Spectroscopy
content: We released PyPAS, a Python package for Doppler Broadening analysis in positron annihilation spectroscopy, including coincidence filtering, 2D analysis, and positron diffusion modeling.

title: SciPAS published in Computer Physics Communications
content: SciPAS, the group's open-source Python package for Positron Annihilation Spectroscopy Doppler Broadening analysis, has been published in Computer Physics Communications. The package provides Coincidence Doppler Broadening filtering, two-dimensional CDB analysis, lineshape parameter computation (S and W), and positron diffusion modelling.

title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
content: A collaboration led by Guy Ron (HUJI) and Efrat Shema (Weizmann Institute) has published a large-scale epigenomic study of breast cancer in Nature. Using CyTOF-based single-cell epigenomics, the team identifies a recurrent basal-like subpopulation hidden inside luminal tumours that carries an aggressive epigenetic signature linked to poor prognosis. Extending this finding to blood, they applied the group's EPINUC single-molecule liquid-biopsy platform to detect early-stage luminal breast cancer from plasma with 95% accuracy and to predict five-year recurrence with 81% accuracy in a multi-institutional cohort. Yishai Arieli (Ron lab) and Christina Riemenschneider are co-first authors.

title: Ynet covers the Nature breast-cancer blood test
content: Ynet (Hebrew) features the group's new Nature paper with the Shema Lab at the Weizmann Institute. The article describes how the Ron group approached the single-molecule EPINUC data as an experimental physics problem, using computational tools to find the epigenetic patterns that flag early breast cancer (95% accuracy for tumours under 2 cm) and predict recurrence. Prof. Guy Ron explains that the more prevalent the aggressive cells' epigenetic signature is in a patient's blood, the higher the risk of relapse, allowing 81% accuracy in separating patients whose cancer returned from those who stayed disease-free.

title: Times of Israel covers the Nature breast-cancer blood test
content: The Times of Israel reports on the group's new Nature paper with the Shema Lab at the Weizmann Institute. The article describes the epigenetic liquid biopsy that detects early-stage breast cancer with 95% accuracy and quotes Prof. Guy Ron on predicting recurrence with 81% accuracy from the epigenetic signature of aggressive tumour cells found in the blood.
